issues.legal_issue: A claimant who denies the true owner’s title and asserts only long possession cannot establish title by adverse possession without pleading and proving possession hostile to the true owner.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s ownership based on an auction purchase was found established, and that finding was not disturbed.
The defendants asserted ancestral and continuous possession and denied that the property had vested in the authority that auctioned it or that the plaintiff owned it.
Some documents showed possession dating from 1963, but the defendants did not plead that their possession was hostile to the true owner.
The plaintiff filed a suit for possession on the basis of title in 1979.
issues.conclusion: The defendants had not established adverse possession; the High Court’s finding that their title had matured by adverse possession was legally unsustainable. The High Court’s judgment was set aside and the suit was decreed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 65 of the Limitation Act, the person claiming title by adverse possession bears the burden of pleading and proving clear and unequivocal facts showing actual, open, peaceful, continuous and hostile possession, with the requisite animus possidendi and knowledge attributable to the true owner. Mere long possession or tax receipts are insufficient. A plea of adverse possession rests on acknowledging that ownership is in another; denying the true owner’s title without pleading possession hostile to that owner does not establish the plea. The Court relied on T. Anjanappa v. Somalingappa, Karnataka Board of Wakf v. Government of India, Kurella Naga Druva Vudaya Bhaskara Rao v. Galla Jani Kamma, Brijesh Kumar v. Shardabai, Chatti Konati Rao v. Palle Venkata Subba Rao, Ravinder Kaur Grewal v. Manjit Kaur, M Siddiq v. Mahant Suresh Das, and the principles in P. Lakshmi Reddy v. L. Lakshmi Reddy and Annakili v. A. Vedanayagam.

rule.if: suit_for_possession_on_title and adverse_possession_claimed and claimant_denied_true_owner_title and not hostile_possession_pleaded

predicates.suit_for_possession_on_title: A claimant brought a suit seeking possession on the basis of title.
predicates.adverse_possession_claimed: The opposing party claimed to have acquired title through adverse possession.
predicates.claimant_denied_true_owner_title: The party claiming adverse possession denied that the identified true owner held title to the property.
predicates.hostile_possession_pleaded: The party claiming adverse possession pleaded that its possession was hostile to the true owner.

issues.definition: When a party defending a title-based possession suit claims adverse possession, denies the true owner’s title, and does not plead possession hostile to that owner, the adverse-possession defence fails.
